item.text:
**6B.5 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**
Overall: **mostly no / mixed**

- There is real evidence of **measurement and process reform** in a few sectors, especially health workforce planning, emergency health review, and procurement digitization.
- But the strongest positive items are mostly **technical, partner-led, or sector-specific**.
- I did **not** find strong evidence that Hasina’s government broadly used transparent correction to fix service delivery across the state.
- The negative evidence is stronger on **opaque crisis management, blame-shifting, and suppression of scrutiny**.

**Accepted claims**

- **Advancing Healthcare Excellence: WHO’s Role in Developing the First National Medical Education Strategy in Bangladesh!** | WHO Bangladesh | 2024-03-04 | URL: https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh | Claim: MOHFW and WHO launched a medical education strategy built on health-workforce studies, evidence-based policy dialogue, and a technical working group to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation. This is the clearest positive evidence of evidence-driven correction in a social-service domain. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.4`, `6B.2`

- **Bangladesh completes its second Joint External Evaluation of the International Health Regulations core capacities** | WHO | 2024-07-11 | URL: https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn | Claim: Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed JEE using the eJEE platform, with 19 technical areas, priority actions, and a consensus-based report; WHO explicitly framed it as a tool for identifying strengths and gaps and guiding future improvement. This is strong evidence of measurement and structured correction. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.2`

- **Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority: public procurement reform / e-GP** | BPPA | 2024-07-24 | URL: https://www.bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1461.html | Claim: BPPA said e-GP made tendering mandatory, integrated e-PMIS and other systems, and increased competition, efficiency, and transparency in procurement. This is solid evidence of process discipline and transparent administration, though indirect for social services. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.4`

- **WHO Bangladesh Celebrates Landmark Success of the Health and Gender Support Project in Cox’s Bazar** | WHO Bangladesh | 2024-06-22 | URL: https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/22-06-2024-who-bangladesh-celebrates-landmark-success-of-the-health-and-gender-support-project-in-cox-s-bazar | Claim: The project was run through the Ministry of Health and World Bank funding, with quantified outputs like 544,000 screenings, trained health workers, and expanded NCD, TB, lab, and EWARS capacity. That is good evidence of measured service delivery improvement in a vulnerable area. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024** | World Bank | 2024-10-01 | URL: https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672 | Claim: The Bank projected rising extreme poverty and more than one Gini-point higher inequality, with subdued investment and unresolved jobs/revenue problems. This undercuts any claim that service-delivery correction was broadly successful in 2024. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

- **Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards** | UN OHCHR | 2024-07-26 | URL: https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights | Claim: The UN said internet shutdowns reduce scrutiny and increase impunity, and called for an impartial, transparent investigation plus security-sector reform. That is strong negative evidence that the government was not using transparent correction during the crisis. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | Reuters | 2024-07-22 | URL: https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153 | Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed opponents rather than pivoting to open correction or accountability. This is strong evidence against transparent, evidence-based crisis management. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

- **Bangladesh repression / security-force abuses discredit elections** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections | Claim: HRW said authorities arrested critics and used repression and violence before the election. This points to a governing style that privileged control over open feedback and correction. | IDs: `6B.5`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

**Search gap**
- I found **clear process evidence** in procurement, medical education, and health-security review.
- I did **not** find strong evidence that Hasina personally used a broad, transparent, feedback-driven correction loop across mainstream social services in 2024.
- The best positives are mostly **partner-led technical reforms** and **narrow sector improvements**; the best negatives show **opacity and coercion** in the year’s major crisis.
